teaser.text: China Life Insurance Company Limited sells financial protection and long-term savings contracts to people and organizations in China. To understand its business, follow the money: customers pay first, China Life invests while promises remain outstanding, and later pays claims, savings benefits, pensions and operating costs.

stock.opening: China Life's probability-weighted forecast reaches HKD32.36 in October 2029, a 39% return including dividends. It hinges on sales costs and persistency.

blocks.heading: Where could China Life's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted forecast is modestly positive over three years. It gives HKD26.02 in October 2027, a 4% return including dividends. It reaches HKD28.89 in October 2028, a 20% return. By October 2029, it reaches HKD32.36, a 39% return.
The final-date range is wide, from HKD16.88 in the bear case to HKD53.62 in the bull case. Today’s price is HKD26.26. The probabilities are 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for China Life?

paragraphs.text: This path reflects retained core earnings, 33.7% growth in first-half 2026 VNB and improved persistency. It does not capitalize the full reported profit surge because first-half net income rose 228.6%, while core earnings rose about 12.7%. The bear case ends at CNY739,700 million after repeated market shocks. The bull case reaches CNY1,077,200 million through stronger retained earnings and higher distributions.

A market reversal during 2027–2028 would push the forecast toward the bear case by reducing investment income, valuation gains and diluted EPS. Lower realized or assumed returns would also weaken VNB and embedded value as policies are priced and reassessed.

dividend.title: China Life dividend: payout and cash coverage
dividend.meta_description: China Life's dividend history, cash coverage, payout outlook and current yield, with the risks that could change future distributions.
dividend.opening: China Life pays CNY0.856 per share in its 2025 total dividend. A simple free-cash-flow test is not meaningful for China Life because policy claims, surrenders, maturities and required capital come first.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines China Life's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does China Life pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend path is CNY1.20 per share in October 2027, CNY1.30 in October 2028 and CNY1.40 in October 2029. The latest interim dividend was CNY0.358 per share, up 50.4% year on year, while the 2025 total was CNY0.856. The bear path falls to CNY0.75 in the second window before a modest recovery. The bull path rises to CNY1.50 and then CNY1.70. The stated rolling three-year distribution floor supports the base path, but it is conditional on profits and distributable reserves.

blocks.heading: What could change China Life's dividend?

paragraphs.text: Solvency updates and annual payout decisions will be decisive. Stronger capital and distributable profits could support the bull dividend path and a narrower valuation discount. Pressure on solvency or distributable earnings would restrain dividends and keep the shares near the bear multiple.

blocks.heading: What is China Life's dividend yield against its price?

paragraphs.text: China Life looks inexpensive, but its headline valuation needs careful interpretation. The P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, compares the share price with profit per share. Its trailing P/E is low, while the forward P/E is higher, implying that expected earnings will fall. The dividend yield offers a more tangible return, but future payments depend on profits, capital needs and board decisions.

earnings.meta_description: China Life next reports are expected October 29, 2026; guidance is broad, and the first full-quarter test after July fee rules is next.
earnings.opening: China Life's next results are expected on October 29, 2026. Watch the first full-quarter test after the July fee rules.
earnings.closing: The full memo also covers China Life's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has China Life guided for 2026–2030?

paragraphs.text: The clearest promise concerns dividends. Over a rolling three years, cash distributions must equal at least 30.0% of average annual distributable profits, if China Life is profitable and has positive accumulated undistributed profit. Distributable profit means profit legally available to shareholders; it is not automatically the same as headline accounting profit.

The broader development plan covers 2026–2030. It calls for core indicators to grow within a “reasonable range”, while improving spending efficiency and risk control. That gives management direction, but no numerical earnings or premium target. The distinction matters: the dividend rule can be tested, while the growth ambition leaves room for judgment.

blocks.heading: Has China Life kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: China Life had promised in 2024 to improve business quality and productivity. New-business value subsequently rose in 2025, which supports that promise, but the measure depends on assumptions about future profits. Policy retention, expenses and investment results must confirm it over time.

blocks.heading: How have China Life's revenue and profit changed?

paragraphs.text: For the first half of 2026, shareholder net income rose 228.6%, while core earnings rose about 12.7%. Core earnings are the company’s own measure, so the reconciliation matters. The gap suggests that investment performance, rather than ordinary insurance service, drove most of the headline increase.

blocks.heading: What should China Life watch in the next results?

paragraphs.text: The period ending September 30, 2026 will provide the first full-quarter test after the July fee rules. Investors should compare new sales with their expense burden and persistence. Slower sales could still represent improvement if policies cost less to acquire and remain in force longer.
